widgets.title: VXLAN initialization errors by host

config.title: VXLAN initialization errors by host
config.description: The VXLAN kernel module or NSX VIBs have failed to load on the host. It is recommended to analyze the hostnames with the highest returned values to look for potential issues. Host preparation is the process in which the NSX Manager 1) installs NSX kernel modules on ESXi hosts that are members of vCenter clusters and 2) builds the NSX control-plane and management-plane fabric. NSX kernel modules packaged in VIB files run within the hypervisor kernel and provide services such as distributed routing, distributed firewall, and VXLAN bridging capabilities. For more information, please see the 'Host Preparation'  and 'VXLAN Preparation' sections in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

If this issue occurs on a stateless host, see 'Deploying VMware NSX for vSphere 6.x through Auto Deploy' (https://kb.vmware.com/kb/2092871 KB 2092871). widgets.title: Distributed firewall errors by severity

config.title: Distributed firewall errors by severity
config.description: In all cases, confirm vsfwd is functioning and that rules are being published to hosts.  Refer to 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide.  Collect the NSX Manager Technical Support Logs (see NSX Administration Guide > Operations and Management > System Events and Audit Logs) To collect the host logs, see the export host-tech-support command in 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide), and open a VMware support request. 301501 -  A host has taken more than 2 minutes to process a firewall configuration update, and the update has timed out. 301503 - Publishing firewall rules has failed for a cluster or one or more hosts. 301506 -  Publishing exclude list updates has failed for a cluster or one or more hosts. 301031 - Parsing and/or updating the firewall configuration has filed for a cluster or one or more hosts. See the key value for context information, including the firewall ruleset generation number.  Confirm that the documented host preparation procedure was followed. Login to the host and collect the /var/log/vsfwd.log file and then force sync the firewall configuration with the REST API https://<nsx-mgr-ip>/api/4.0/firewall/forceSync/<host-id>. (See 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide.) If the Distributed Firewall configuration still fails to be updated on the host, collect the NSX Manager Technical Support Logs (see NSX Administration Guide > Operations and Management > System Events and Audit Logs) and the ESXi host logs (see the export host-tech-support command in 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide), and open a VMware support request.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: SpoofGuard errors by severity

config.title: SpoofGuard errors by severity
config.description: SpoofGuard errors can occur at the NSX Manager layer or at the host vnic layer.    Events at the NSX Manager layer: 301502 - A host has taken more than 2 minutes to process a Spoof Guard configuration update, and the update has timed out. 301505 - Publishing Spoof Guard updates has failed for a cluster or one or more hosts. Events at the host vnic layer: 301061 - Failed to receive/parse/update SpoofGuard configuration.  The key value will report the ruleset generation number and other debugging details.  301062 - Failed to apply SpoofGuard to vNIC.  301064 - Failed to disable SpoofGuard on vNIC.   In all cases, confirm vsfwd is functioning and that rules are being published to hosts.  Refer to 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide.  Collect the NSX Manager Technical Support Logs (see NSX Administration Guide > Operations and Management > System Events and Audit Logs) To collect the host logs, see the export host-tech-support command in 'Troubleshooting Distributed Firewall' in the NSX Troubleshooting Guide), and open a VMware support request. Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Distributed firewall rule set config errors by severity

config.title: Distributed firewall rule set config errors by severity
config.description: Distributed firewall configuration errors by severity of event. 301001 - Host failed to receive/parse filter config or open device /dev/dvfiltertbl. This event is not expected.  Refer to the key-value pair for context and failure reason, which may include VIB version mismatch between NSX Manager and prepared hosts and unexpected upgrade issues. 301002 - Firewall config failed to be applied to the vNIC.  Refer to the key-value pair for context and failure reason. This event is expected with Service Insertion. Collect the ESXi host and NSX Manager logs and open a VMware support request.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Service Composer service profile errors by severity

config.title: Service Composer service profile errors by severity
config.description: Service Composer helps you provision and assign network and security services to applications in a virtual infrastructure. This widget reports on service profile configuration issues. During service deployment in NSX, a third party vendor selects the service category for the service being deployed. A default service profile is created for each vendor template. 301011 - a host failed to parse a service profile config or open a VSIP device. Refer to the key-value pair for failure reason and context. 301012 - a service profile configuration failed to be updated. Refer to the key value for context information, such as profile name and version.  301014 - a service profile configuration failed to be deleted. Refer to the key value for context information, such as profile name and version.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Flow missed errors

widgets.title: Edge VM events by severity

config.title: Edge VM events by severity
config.description: All of the Edge VM events.  Some of the events are expected to be self-correcting.  The events more likely to indicate an issue include: - Event 30102 - Edge VM needs a force sync. An automatic force sync is triggered when a problematic state is detected.  If the automatic force sync fails, try a manual force sync via by going to NSX Edges > Action > Force Sync.  Note - Force sync is a disruptive operation and reboots the Edge VMs.The Edge VM  - Event 30032 - Edge VM cannot be found in the vCenter inventory and likely has been deleted directly from vCenter; this is not a supported operation as NSX managed objects must be added or deleted from the vSphere Web Client interface for NSX.  To recover, deploy a new Edge. Look at the https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-NSX-Data-Center-for-vSphere/6.3/com.vmware.nsx.logging.doc/GUID-4CAA25F7-1EE7-4B8A-957E-52865F723C10.html NSX Edge System Events documentations for the details. For more information, refer to http://kb.vmware.com/kb/2137685 KB 2137685.

widgets.title: Edge HA events by severity

config.title: Edge HA events by severity
config.description: NSX Edge High Availability ensures that the services provided by NSX Edge appliances are available even when a hardware or software failure renders a single appliance unavailable.    This widget indicates a change to the HA environment -- either that HA has been disabled or enabled or that an HA failover has occurred. 30202 - Explanation: An HA failover has occurred, and the secondary NSX Edge VM has transitioned from the STANDBY to ACTIVE state.  Action: No action is required. 30203 - Explanation: An HA failover has occurred, and the primary NSX Edge VM has transitioned from the ACTIVE to STANDBY state.  Action: No action is required. 30039 - NSX Edge HighAvailability is enabled. 30040 - NSX Edge HighAvailability is disabled. Look at the https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-NSX-Data-Center-for-vSphere/6.3/com.vmware.nsx.logging.doc/GUID-4CAA25F7-1EE7-4B8A-957E-52865F723C10.html NSX Edge System Events documentations for the details.

widgets.title: VMWare NSX VM connection failure - As reported by Host

config.title: VMWare NSX VM connection failure - As reported by Host
config.description: The Guest Introspection host module failed to connect to the Guest Introspection VM on the reporting host.  A corresponding system event reporting loss of Guest Introspection VM also may be seen.  A service ID of 100 will be reported for the Guest Introspection VM. Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: VM connected - As reported by Host

config.title: VM connected - As reported by Host
config.description: A connection between the Guest Introspection VM and the Guest Introspection Module has been established.  This alert is expected when bringing up a host or when an existing host brings up the Guest Introspection VM (for example, after a host or Virtual Center reboot).  Rebooting Virtual Center may trigger ESX Agent Manager (EAM) to reboot the Guest Introspection VM if it times out waiting for the Guest Introspection VM status from the host.  Such time-outs may happen in large-scale deployments when Virtual Center is too busy processing other events to respond.

widgets.title: Host Module Report Missed From Host - Reported by NSX Manager

config.title: Host Module Report Missed From Host - Reported by NSX Manager
config.description: NSX Manager did not receive the MUX report from the host's Guest Introspection Module.  Reasons to investigate immediately include: - the Guest Introspection service is down - the Guest Introspection module on the host itself is having issues.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Host Module Connected to NSX Manager - Reported by NSX Manager

config.title: Host Module Connected to NSX Manager - Reported by NSX Manager
config.description: This widget captures the event of Guest Introspection Module connecting to NSX Manager. This event log may be triggered when a new host is connecting for the first time or if an existing host had disconnected before and re-connecting back again. For existing host, match the hits on this widget with the hits on the 'Guest Introspection Module Report Missed From Host - Reported by NSX Manager' widget which reports down event.

widgets.title: Server Activity Monitoring report Missing - Reported by NSX Manager

config.title: Server Activity Monitoring report Missing - Reported by NSX Manager
config.description: The Server Access Monitoring report was not received by NSX Manager.  The Guest Introspection module delivers this report to NSX Manager.  This error suggests an issue with the Guest Introspection module or VM.  Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Partner Service VM connection failure - Reported by Host

config.title: Partner Service VM connection failure - Reported by Host
config.description: This event is to monitor the connection down between the Guest Introspection Module and the Partner Solution VM. This will be sorted by reporting ESXi host.  Service ID != 100 for Partner Service VMs. Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.

widgets.title: Partner Service VM connected to Guest Introspection Module - Reported by Host

config.title: Partner Service VM connected to Guest Introspection Module - Reported by Host
config.description: This log is generated when the connection between Partner Service VM and the Guest Introspection Module is established. This may be generated 1) when bringing up a new partner solution or 2) when existing host brings up the Partner Service VM (possibly after the VM or host reboot or vCenter reboot). vCenter reboot may result in Partner Service VM to reboot. This reboot is triggered by  ESX Agent Manager if it times-out on receiving the Partner Service VMs status on a host. Possible reason may be that vCenter is too busy after a reboot especially in large scale deployment.

Please refer to Operations for Logs documentation to learn more about Agent Groups. Note: In healthy environments this widget should return no results.
